prompt: Training runs all positions in parallel; generation runs one at a time. Why do the two compute the same thing?

options.A: Both use the same temperature
options.B: The causal mask makes each position see only itself and earlier positions, exactly what it sees during generation
options.C: They don't; models are adjusted after training to match
options.D: Generation retrains the model after each token

prompt: Training compute ≈ 6 × parameters × tokens. A 70B model on 15 trillion tokens. How many operations, in units of 10²⁴?
SFT scores only the answer tokens (weight 0 on the template and prompt). What would go wrong if it scored the prompt too?

options.A: The causal mask would stop working
options.B: The model would forget the vocabulary
options.C: Nothing; it only costs a little more compute
options.D: Training effort would go into predicting user messages, so the model learns to write prompts as well as answers

prompt: Quantizing weights to 8-bit gives decode “two multiplying wins”. What are they?

options.A: Each tick reads half the weight bytes, and the freed memory holds more KV caches, so the batch grows
options.B: Fewer layers and a smaller vocabulary
options.C: Shorter prompts and shorter answers
options.D: Lower temperature and less sampling

prompt: Why is it safe to reuse a stored KV prefix for a different request?

options.A: Keys and values at position i depend only on tokens 1…i (the causal mask), so an identical prefix always gives identical KV
options.B: KV values are the same for every prompt
options.C: The server re-checks every value against the new request
options.D: It isn't fully safe; small errors are accepted for speed

prompt: How is the causal mask applied in code?

options.A: Set the attention weights to 0 after the weighted average
options.B: Add −∞ to the scores above the diagonal before softmax, so future positions get exactly 0 weight
options.C: Delete the future tokens from the input
options.D: Multiply the values of future tokens by 0.5

prompt: When would the cost gap between output and input tokens shrink? Pick all that apply.

options.A: Longer contexts per request
options.B: Larger decode batches, so each weight read is shared by more users
options.C: Quantized weights, so each tick reads fewer bytes
options.D: Smaller KV caches (shorter contexts, fewer KV heads), so more users fit in a batch

prompt: In a chat app, which latency does a user notice first?

options.A: TTFT: how long before anything appears
options.B: End-to-end latency
options.C: Time to compute the KV cache size
options.D: Throughput across all users

prompt: You raise the decode batch from 1 to 64. What happens?

options.A: Total tokens per second rises a lot; each user's TPOT rises a little; KV memory eventually caps how many users fit
options.B: Throughput stays the same; each user gets slower
options.C: Each user's TPOT stays exactly the same until compute runs out
options.D: Both throughput and each user's TPOT get better

prompt: Prefill floor: 2 operations per parameter per token. A 70B model on GPUs delivering 1,978 trillion operations per second in total. Minimum TTFT for a 2,000-token prompt, in milliseconds?
Which backend pattern is prompt caching most like?

options.A: A write-through cache in front of a database
options.B: Database sharding
options.C: A content-addressed cache with a TTL: hash the prefix blocks, look them up, expire entries after minutes
options.D: A message queue

prompt: TTFT is 0.3 s and TPOT is 25 ms. How many seconds until a 401-token answer has fully arrived?
A 70B model on 2 H100s at 16-bit misses its TPOT target and fits only a few users. Which fix keeps quality but adds communication overhead and a bigger minimum deployment?

options.A: Quantizing to 8-bit
options.B: Lowering the temperature
options.C: Raising the batch size
options.D: Adding GPUs (tensor parallelism): more bandwidth per tick and more room for caches

prompt: Which backend pattern is decode batching most like?

options.A: Read replicas
options.B: Group commit: many transactions share one disk flush, so each waits slightly longer but total throughput rises
options.C: A CDN edge cache
options.D: A circuit breaker

prompt: Loss = −ln p(correct token). The model gives the correct token 50%. What is the loss?
You ask a base model (pre-training only) “What is a river bank?” What is it most likely to do?

options.A: Return an error
options.B: Refuse, because it has no instructions
options.C: Answer politely like a chat assistant
options.D: Continue the text as a document would, perhaps with more quiz questions, rather than answer

prompt: Which are real differences between training and serving infrastructure? Pick all that apply.

options.A: Serving updates the weights after every request
options.B: One failed GPU stalls a whole synchronized training job, so teams checkpoint often
options.C: Training GPUs must exchange gradients every step, so the network and stragglers matter as much as the chips
options.D: Training needs several times the memory per parameter (gradients and optimizer state)
options.E: Training uses a KV cache to skip recomputation

prompt: Which backend idea is the causal mask most like?

options.A: A snapshot read: each transaction sees only what was committed before it, never later writes
options.B: A dead-letter queue
options.C: Rate limiting
options.D: A load balancer

prompt: Same formula, but the model gives the correct token only 1%. What is the loss?
What does a chat template do?

options.A: Stores past conversations on the server
options.B: Adds a second model that handles conversation
options.C: Translates the prompt into a fixed format of questions
options.D: Wraps each turn in special tokens (like <|user|>, <|assistant|>) and flattens the messages list into one token string the model continues

prompt: Llama 2 used about 27,540 written SFT examples versus about 2 trillion pre-training tokens. What does that say?

options.A: SFT replaces most of what pre-training learned
options.B: SFT examples are worth more than pre-training tokens for learning facts
options.C: Knowledge comes from pre-training; a small, high-quality post-training set mainly shapes behavior and format
options.D: Pre-training is mostly wasted

prompt: Base model vs chat model after supervised fine-tuning (SFT): what changes?

options.A: Only the weight values, through more training with the same next-token loss on curated prompt → answer pairs; architecture, tokenizer and loss stay the same
options.B: The tokenizer is retrained for dialogue
options.C: A new answer-generation layer is added
options.D: The loss function is replaced by a reward

prompt: Why does an output token cost more GPU time than an input token?

options.A: Output tokens go through more layers
options.B: Output tokens are longer than input tokens
options.C: Providers charge more for output to discourage long answers; GPU time is the same
options.D: Input tokens are processed together in prefill, with the GPU's math fully busy; each output step reads all the weights and caches to emit just one token per user

prompt: Which levers lower cost per million tokens? Pick all that apply.

options.A: More tokens per second while busy (batching, quantization, better kernels)
options.B: A bigger vocabulary
options.C: Lower temperature
options.D: A higher busy share of each paid hour (traffic, autoscaling, sharing GPUs across models)

prompt: Two GPUs at $4 per GPU-hour produce 1,000 output tokens per second. What is the cost per million output tokens, in dollars?
On a cache hit for that 3,000-token prefix, what improves? Pick all that apply.

options.A: TPOT: each output token gets much faster
options.B: TTFT: only the new tokens need prefill
options.C: Input cost: providers bill cached input tokens at a discount
options.D: The answer gets more accurate

prompt: What would the model learn if you trained without the causal mask?

options.A: Nothing: training would crash
options.B: To generate whole sentences at once
options.C: Exactly the same thing, only slower
options.D: To copy the next token from the input, since it could see it; at generation time that token doesn't exist yet, so the trick fails

prompt: Quantization speeds up decode a lot but prefill much less. Why?

options.A: Quantization only applies to output tokens
options.B: Prefill is already cached
options.C: Decode is memory-bound, so fewer bytes per weight means a faster tick; prefill is compute-bound, so it gains only if the GPU also does the math in lower precision
options.D: Prefill doesn't use the weights

prompt: Run those 6.3 × 10²⁴ operations on 8,192 GPUs at 989 trillion operations per second each, with 40% utilization. How many days?
The DPO loss is −ln σ(gap). What is the “gap”?

options.A: How much more the model now favors the chosen answer over the rejected one, compared with the starting model
options.B: The reward model's score difference
options.C: The number of tokens the two answers differ by
options.D: The difference in length between the two answers

prompt: RLHF vs DPO: what does each need?

options.A: Both need a reward model; DPO just trains it faster
options.B: RLHF: only human-written answers. DPO: a reward model
options.C: RLHF: a trained reward model plus reinforcement learning with generation during training. DPO: one loss directly on chosen/rejected pairs, ordinary supervised training
options.D: RLHF trains on single answers; DPO needs a full conversation

prompt: An app sends a 3,000-token system prompt plus a short user message. How should it order the prompt to keep prompt-cache hits?

options.A: Order doesn't matter; the cache matches any shared text
options.B: User message first so it gets the most attention
options.C: Fixed content first (system prompt, tools, examples), changing content (user message, timestamps) last
options.D: Put a timestamp at the top so the cache knows the prompt's age

prompt: An H100 does about 989 trillion operations per second and reads about 3.35 trillion bytes per second. How many operations can it do per byte read before memory stops being the bottleneck?

options.A: There is no difference in what the model learns
options.B: −ln p is cheaper to compute
options.C: −ln p punishes confident wrong answers without limit (p → 0 gives loss → ∞), while 1 − p caps the penalty at 1
options.D: 1 − p can be negative

prompt: Pre-training on one 1,000-token document. How many next-token training examples does it give?

options.A: −ln p for every token

options.C: 1 for the correct token, 0 for all others
options.D: The same value for every token
